Prototype and light-duty use only

Larger threads are a more realistic starting point. Print one and check the fit gently.

For a chair, table joint, wall fixing, or other load-bearing connection, get the correct metal screw. This model has no tested strength or tightening torque.

MATCH FIRST

Same diameter isn’t enough.

Check pitch, length, head clearance and drive size. Furniture screws may be self-tapping or proprietary. This tool makes a blunt, fully threaded machine screw with an approximate 60° profile.

PRINT ONE

Start with a fit test.

Import the STL in millimetres at 100% scale. Head-down orientation is supplied for convenience; layer direction affects strength. Try fine layers, keep supports off threads, and never force a tight fit.

KNOW THE LIMIT

Plastic isn’t a metal spare.

Small threads and repeated tightening are difficult. Resin or SLS can capture finer detail, but material and process still determine durability. Read the printing guidance ↗

STL contains geometry, not printer settings or guaranteed tolerances. Metric thread reference ↗
